entries.english:
A file volume from the middle of the sixteenth century, entitled ‘Groß gebrochen L. Report book concerning various affairs between Mainz and the Palatinate. NB miscellanea.’

Contents: Amicable award between Archbishop Konrad of Mainz and Pfalzgraf Otto I of Mosbach, concerning, among other matters, the following disputes: the court at (Groß-?)Rinderfeld and the monastery of Aschaffenburg's Hub court there; the church's serfs at St Martin's in Tauberbischofsheim, in the district of Werbach, at Osterburken and Königshofen, and the king's people at Lohrbach and Reichenbuch; high jurisdiction at Distelhausen; dues and tithes at Lauda and Königshofen; escort rights from Osterburken to Wimpfen and along the Bergstraße; Mainz's hunting ban at Trienz (1425) (folios 3–21).

Complaint by Pfalzgraf Georg, provost of Mainz Cathedral and Bischof von Speyer, that the Electoral Palatinate has recently imposed a gulden toll at Oberheimbach, a place belonging to the cathedral chapter (undated, after 1513) (folios 22–25). Report by Philipp Echter von Mespelbrunn der Ältere, Vizedom zu Aschaffenburg, on disputes with the Electoral Palatinate arising within the Vizedom's jurisdiction, including the driving of livestock by the inhabitants of Radheim to Wenigumstadt and whether the farm at Dorndiel belonged to the district of (Groß-)Ostheim (1526) (folios 26–27). List of matters negotiated by the councillors of Mainz and the Electoral Palatinate at Mainz on 1 July 1533, including disputes over Osthofen and Schefflenz, the parish of the Aschaffenburg monastery at (Groß-?)Umstadt, and St Rupert's monastery near Bingen (1533) (folios 28–31). Correspondence between Elector Ludwig V of the Palatinate and Archbishop of Mainz Cardinal Albrecht concerning the punishment of Palatine subjects, especially in the district of Amorbach, after suppression of the Peasants' Revolt (1529/1530) (folios 32–45).

Correspondence concerning the tax demanded by the Mainz district count at Mudau from the king's people at Lohrbach, Auerbach, Dallu and Rittersbach, who were also tenants of the Teutonic Order and the Electoral Palatinate (undated, sixteenth century) (folios 46–51); list of the ‘burning ransom’ levied in the district of Mudau (undated, sixteenth century) (folios 52 and 56–57); letter from Rab von Liebenstein, official at (Nieder-)Olm and (Gau-)Algesheim, concerning the taxation of Palatine serfs at Gau-Bickelheim (1534) (folios 53–55); complaint by the inhabitants of Allfeld and Katzental about the Electoral Palatinate's new demand for travel money and other dues (undated, sixteenth century) (folios 57–61); report by the official of Gau-Algesheim concerning disputes with the Electoral Palatinate around Dromersheim, Dietersheim, Bingen, and Gau-Algesheim, including the landwehr, toll, escort, and serfs (undated, sixteenth century) (folios 62–63); report by the official and steward at Amorbach and Mudau concerning disputes with the Electoral Palatinate at Balsbach, Wagenschwend, and Laudenberg (undated, sixteenth century) (folios 64–64 verso); report on disputes with the Electoral Palatinate over the Rhine meadows between Walluf and Kaub (folios 65–67); report by the Rheingau land clerk on various Palatine complaints, including fishing rights in the Nahe (folios 68–69); letter from Wernnher zum Jungen concerning the Eiswasser, partly sold to Electoral Mainz, and fishing near Biebesheim in 1427, copied in the sixteenth century from ‘the first book of Conrad, folio 302’ (folio 70); petition by Johannes Vyscher, vicar of the collegiate church ad gradus BMV at Mainz, concerning revenues withheld from him by the Electoral Palatinate at Wackernheim (folios 71); lists of Mainz fiefs granted to the families von Dalberg, Lander von Sponheim, and Schlieder in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries (folios 72–76).

Reports by the official of Gau-Algesheim concerning disputes with the Electoral Palatinate, including tolls at Kempten, Ockenheim, and (Nieder-)Olm and the village of Dietersheim (folios 77–81); report by the toll clerk at Ehrenfels on various Palatine complaints (folios 82); list of inhabitants of Altheim near Dieburg refusing the land tax and the resulting expenses (1492) (folios 83–92); petition by the subjects of Rodau concerning grazing rights disputed with the community of Bensheim (folios 93); summary of disputes with the Electoral Palatinate in the district of Gernsheim, including the toll there, fishing on the Rhine, and the boundary dispute between Rodau and Bensheim (folios 94–96); complaint by the provost of St Alban near Mainz that Palatine officials infringed his jurisdiction over Bodenheim (folios 97–98); list of disputes in 1523 concerning the spiritual jurisdiction of the Archbishop of Mainz (priestly estates, appointments to parishes, subsidy payments, and synodal court) in these Palatine places: Ober- and Nieder-Ingelheim, Schwabenheim, Nieder-Saulheim, Erbes-Büdesheim, Sprendlingen, Friesenheim, Dalheim, Köngernheim, Oppenheim, Nierstein, (Gau-)Weinheim, Wolfsheim, Aspisheim, Sponsheim, Essenheim, Stadecken, and Engelstadt (1523) (folios 98–100); list of Rhine meadows between Walluf and Kempten and Mainz's fishing rights there (folios 101–104); grant by Archbishop Adolf of Mainz of fishing rights in the Nahe near Bingen to the collegiate church ad gradus BMV at Mainz (1472) (folios 105–108); arbitration in the dispute between the officials at Buchen, Amorbach Abbey, and the hereditary leaseholder of the Helmstheim farm (Altheim near Buchen) concerning timber for construction and rents accruing there (1526) (folios 109–112); arbitration awards, letters, etc. concerning disputes between Konrad von Dottenheim and Hans von Rosenberg over Oberschüpf, Kupprichhausen, Lengenrieden, and Uiffingen, and report on the transfer of Sachsenflur and Dainbach to the Electoral Palatinate (1529) (folios 113–120); report by Hans von Adelsheim, official at Wildenburg, on negotiations with the Vogt zu Mosbach concerning disputed ‘heg schleg’ and ditches (1533) (folios 121–122); complaint by Mathis Schuhmacher of Oberschefflenz about his unjust punishment by the Vogt zu Mosbach (folios 123); copies of several grants by the city of Mainz (1401, 1406, 1407, 1409, 1418) of various municipal revenues, with which Ulrich Salzkern of Alzey endowed a perpetual alms founded at Heidelberg in 1412 and Friedrich Lodenter, custodian of the Neumünster collegiate church at Würzburg, endowed Heidelberg University in 1409 (folios 124–145).

Reports by Hans von Adelsheim, official at Wildenburg, on various Palatine complaints, including disputed forest, fishing, and sheep-driving rights in and near Limbach, jurisdiction over Ober-, Mittel-, and Unterschefflenz, and the gulden toll levied there by the Electoral Palatinate (1534) (folios 146–151); extracts from correspondence between Electoral Palatinate and Electoral Mainz concerning disputed fishing rights in the Nahe near Bingen and from accounts of the Rheingau land clerk, 1431–1500 (folios 152–157); copies of deeds concerning sales of vineyards at Bingen at ‘uff der rawehelden’ (1432), ‘am rodeborn’ (1492), and ‘am kamberg’ (1460, 1467), and copy of a 1438 lease issued by St Rupert's monastery to the miller of its ‘Frauenmühle’ (folios 158–166); report by Martin Kraft, toll clerk at Gernsheim, to the Mainz cathedral chapter (with an attached sketch) concerning its dispute with the Electoral Palatinate over the dyke at Biblis (folios 167–170); report by the council of Bingen responding to various complaints of the Mainz cathedral chapter (folios 171–177).

Correspondence on collection of the Turkish tax in 1545, especially reports on the rights of the Mainz cathedral chapter and various Mainz collegiate churches and monasteries in individual places, where Palatine serfs living there resist assessment. The following places are named: Osthofen; Oberheimbach, Finthen, Gonsenheim, Eddersheim (Mainz cathedral provostry); Mombach (Mainz cathedral chapter); Nackenheim, Büdesheim, Bubenheim near Engelstadt, Münsterliederbach, Heidesheim (St Stephen's collegiate church at Mainz); Bodenheim (St Alban's collegiate church near Mainz); Bretzenheim, Zahlbach (Mariendalen monastery at Mainz); Heidesheim, Budenheim (Altenmünster monastery at Mainz); Zornheim (St Clare's monastery at Mainz) (1545) (folios 178–198).
